pdf_claim: Seminary Ridge barricade in the small wood in front of Schmucker Hall: fences dismantled and rails stacked into a barricade that curved through the wood, about 600 yd long (Wikipedia), held by I Corps remnants and Wainwright's artillery (20 guns Wikipedia, 22 in four batteries HistoryNet); built Jul 1 afternoon before about 16:00, overrun about 16:00-16:30; no start time, no crew list.
corrected_claim: A breastwork of rails, stumps and earth stood immediately west of the Seminary building on Jul 1. Doubleday ordered Robinson's division to intrench on its arrival and Robinson set Paul's First Brigade (16th Maine, 94th NY, 104th NY, 13th Mass., 107th Pa.) to work; the work was done between about 11:00 and about 13:00 (bounds from Baxter's arrival at 11 a.m. and the 16th Maine leaving for the right at about one o'clock), and other troops had added rails earlier in the day. Hunt counts 22 guns in four batteries on the line (16 concentrated plus Stewart's six), Wainwright counts twelve concentrated; the 20 of the PDF is not supported. Length (about 600 yd), the curve and the dismantling of a 600-yd fence line are not in any source and stay marked gaps; the form is a conflict (circular redoubt vs a line parallel to the Seminary). Wave 4 (2026-11-14): two secondary books give a circular or semicircular plan (Small 1886: 'redoubt of earth and fence rails, in a circular form'; Toombs 1888: 'semicircular line of breast works') against McFarland's line through the west edge of the grove; Bates 1875 says the work was ordered as the line to which the division could fall back; the hour it was turned is carried as Cooper 'after 4 p.m.', Pender 'about 4 o'clock', NPS 'by about 5:00 p.m.'. The 600 yd length stays unsupported.
